title: Distance and Midpoint Formulas
seo_title: Distance and Midpoint Formula Worksheet (Geometry, G-GPE.B.7) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on the distance and midpoint formulas: radical answers, missing endpoints, partitioning a segment, and perimeter and area. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The midpoint averages the coordinates: ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2).
body_html:
How it works

The distance formula is the Pythagorean theorem on the coordinate plane. The horizontal change and the vertical change are the legs of a right triangle, and the distance is the hypotenuse:

d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²)

The midpoint formula averages the coordinates: M = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2).

To find a point that is a fraction of the way from A to B, add that fraction of the change to A.

Example

Find the distance between (−2, 3) and (4, −5).

Changes: 4 − (−2) = 6 and −5 − 3 = −8

d = √(36 + 64) = √100

Answer: 10

Example

M(1, 4) is the midpoint of AB, and A is (−3, 7). Find B.

From A to M: +4 across, −3 down

Take the same step again from M: (1 + 4, 4 − 3)

Answer: B(5, 1)

Common mistakes

  • Adding the changes: √(6² + 8²) is 10, not 6 + 8 = 14.
  • Forgetting the square root. 100 is d², not d.
  • Subtracting in the midpoint formula. The midpoint is an average, so add, then divide by 2.
  • Giving the midpoint when the question asks for the other endpoint.

faq.a: d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²). It comes from the Pythagorean theorem, with the horizontal and vertical changes as the legs.
M = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2). Average the x-coordinates and average the y-coordinates.

faq.q: How do you find an endpoint from the midpoint?
faq.a: Double the midpoint and subtract the known endpoint: B = 2M − A, for each coordinate.

faq.q: How do you partition a segment in a ratio a : b?
faq.a: The point is a/(a + b) of the way from A to B. Multiply the change in each coordinate by a/(a + b) and add it to A.

items.e: d = √((−7 − 1)² + (−3 − (−2))²) = √((−8)² + (−1)²) = √(64 + 1) = √65. 65 has no perfect square factor, so the answer is √65.

sets.title: Perimeter and area on the coordinate plane

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 1 mile. Home is at (1, −3) and school is at (13, 13). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(12² + 16²) = 20 units. Each unit is 1 mile, so the distance is 20 miles.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 1 mile. The gym is at (−3, 1) and the mall is at (6, 13). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(9² + 12²) = 15 units. Each unit is 1 mile, so the distance is 15 miles.

items.q: Find the area of triangle PQR with P(−4, −5), Q(1, −5) and R(−2, −2).
items.e: Base PQ is horizontal: 5 units. Height is the vertical distance from R to the base: 3 units. Area = ½ × 5 × 3 = 7.5 square units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−6, −1), B(−2, −1), C(−2, 2), D(−6, 2). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 4 and BC = 3 (count or subtract coordinates). Perimeter = 2(4 + 3) = 14 units.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 0.5 mile. The library is at (2, −4) and the park is at (7, 8). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(5² + 12²) = 13 units. Each unit is 0.5 mile, so the distance is 6.5 miles.

items.q: Find the area of triangle PQR with P(−1, −5), Q(3, −5) and R(0, −2).
items.e: Base PQ is horizontal: 4 units. Height is the vertical distance from R to the base: 3 units. Area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 square units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−3, −3), B(−1, −3), C(−1, 3), D(−3, 3). Find its area.
items.e: AB = 2 and BC = 6 (count or subtract coordinates). Area = 2 × 6 = 12 square units.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 1 mile. Home is at (3, 2) and school is at (12, 14). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(9² + 12²) = 15 units. Each unit is 1 mile, so the distance is 15 miles.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 1 mile. The bus station is at (0, 2) and the museum is at (9, 14). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(9² + 12²) = 15 units. Each unit is 1 mile, so the distance is 15 miles.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(−6, −6), B(−3, −6) and C(−6, −2). Find its area.
items.e: The legs are AB = 3 and AC = 4, and they are perpendicular. Area = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 square units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−3, −5), B(1, −5), C(1, −2), D(−3, −2). Find its area.
items.e: AB = 4 and BC = 3 (count or subtract coordinates). Area = 4 × 3 = 12 square units.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 0.5 mile. Home is at (−3, 3) and school is at (0, 7). What is the straight-line distance between them?
items.e: Distance on the map: √(3² + 4²) = 5 units. Each unit is 0.5 mile, so the distance is 2.5 miles.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, −3), B(3, −3) and C(0, 1). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 3, AC = 4. BC = √(3² + 4²) = 5 by the distance formula. Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 units.

items.q: Find the area of triangle PQR with P(−5, −2), Q(0, −2) and R(−2, 1).
items.e: Base PQ is horizontal: 5 units. Height is the vertical distance from R to the base: 3 units. Area = ½ × 5 × 3 = 7.5 square units.

items.q: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, −1), B(6, −1) and C(0, 7). Find its perimeter.
items.e: AB = 6, AC = 8. BC = √(6² + 8²) = 10 by the distance formula. Perimeter = 6 + 8 + 10 = 24 units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−5, −1), B(−3, −1), C(−3, 5), D(−5, 5). Find its area.
items.e: AB = 2 and BC = 6 (count or subtract coordinates). Area = 2 × 6 = 12 square units.

items.q: Rectangle ABCD has vertices A(−6, −5), B(−1, −5), C(−1, −3), D(−6, −3). Find its area.
items.e: AB = 5 and BC = 2 (count or subtract coordinates). Area = 5 × 2 = 10 square units.

items.q: On a town map, each unit is 1 mile. The bus station is at (−2, 0) and the museum is at (1, 4). What is the straight-line distance between them?
